evidence.finding: Every interval from 09:15 through 11:45 was reported exactly 26.0 percentage points below answered_within_threshold / (offered_calls - short_abandoned_calls); earlier intervals matched the formula.
Recalculated service level was below 80% only at 09:15 and 09:45 and remained at least 85% from 10:00 onward, contradicting the displayed sustained degradation.
Incident-period offered volume averaged only 0.18% above forecast, with alternating positive and negative interval variances rather than a sustained surge.
All 49 scheduled agents remained logged in; productive staffing stayed at 45–46, adherence remained between 91.84% and 93.88%, and no agents were in training.
Account Support showed localized degradation, but Billing improved and General Service remained strong; unchanged queue staffing and divergent outcomes do not explain the uniform aggregate offset.
No platform, routing, or other operational event was recorded during the incident-and-after window.

primary_root_cause_detail: Beginning exactly at the 09:15 incident boundary, the reported service-level field became 26.0 percentage points lower than the value calculated using the supplied metric definition. The fixed discrepancy persisted through all 11 incident intervals, creating a sustained below-target dashboard alert even though recalculated service recovered from 10:00 onward.
recommended_actions: Correct the dashboard calculation or transformation applying the 26-point downward offset and backfill affected intervals from 09:15 onward.
Add automated reconciliation between reported service level and an independent calculation from component counts.
Monitor Account Support separately and rebalance capacity if its localized service deterioration recurs.
Preserve interval-level validation alerts so reporting defects are distinguished from genuine operational misses.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Volume averaged only 0.18% above forecast during the incident; isolated elevated intervals cannot explain a fixed 26-point reporting offset.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained 49, with productive staffing stable at 45–46 and no training-related capacity loss.
Incident-period AHT averaged 0.59% below forecast and was 3.24% below forecast at onset, so no sustained increase preceded the alert.
Localized queue variation contributed to brief genuine misses, but queue staffing was unchanged and the variation cannot produce the identical aggregate reporting discrepancy.
No platform event was recorded, recalculated service recovered, and queues did not exhibit a broad simultaneous collapse.

stakeholder_summary: CC-012 was a confirmed dashboard data-quality incident rather than a sustained center-wide service failure. An exact 26-point reporting understatement began at 09:15. Genuine service misses were brief, and recalculated service remained at or above 85% from 10:00 onward. Demand, AHT, staffing, queue-wide imbalance, and platform disruption were not primary causes.
